over a\n            // random password that no account can hold. A hand-written constant here was the\n            // classic failure mode: if it does not parse, verify() returns before the KDF runs and\n            // the unknown-account branch silently becomes free -- which is the very leak the\n            // constant was meant to close. dummyEncoded() is verified to parse below for that\n            // reason, and AuthServiceTest re-checks it by timing the branch.\n            this.dummyPassword = randomChars(24);\n            this.dummyEncoded = encode(this.dummyPassword);\n            if (StoredDigest.parse(this.dummyEncoded) == null) {\n                throw new IllegalStateException(\"internal error: generated dummy digest does not parse\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        /** Real encoded digest that belongs to no account; used to charge unknown accounts. */\n        String dummyEncoded() {\n            return dummyEncoded;\n        }\n\n        String encode(char[] password) {\n            PasswordRules.rejectForEnrolment(password).ifPresent(reason -> {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"cannot store this password: \" + reason);\n            });\n            byte[] salt = new byte[SALT_BYTES];\n            random.nextBytes(salt);\n            byte[] digest = derive(password, salt, iterations);\n            try {\n                return PREFIX + \"$\" + iterations\n                        + \"$\" + Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(salt)\n                        + \"$\" + Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(digest);\n            } finally {\n                Arrays.fill(digest, (byte) 0);\n            }\n        }\n\n        /**\n         * Derives once and compares. Always costs one full derivation, whatever the state of the\n         * inputs: an unparsable stored digest is charged against the dummy parameters, and a\n         * candidate that may not be hashed is replaced by {@link #dummyPassword}.\n         */\n        Verification verify(char[] candidate, String storedDigest) {\n            StoredDigest stored = StoredDigest.parse(storedDigest);\n            boolean candidateUsable = PasswordRules.rejectCandidate(candidate).isEmpty();\n\n            char[] effective = candidateUsable ? candidate : dummyPassword;\n            byte[] salt = stored != null ? stored.salt : dummySaltOfDummy();\n            int rounds = stored != null ? stored.iterations : iterations;\n\n            byte[] derived = derive(effective, salt, rounds);\n            try {\n                boolean matched = candidateUsable && stored != null\n                        && MessageDigest.isEqual(stored.digest, derived);\n                String error = stored != null ? null\n                        : (storedDigest == null ? \"absent-record\" : StoredDigest.lastParseError());\n                return new Verification(matched, error, rounds);\n            } finally {\n                Arrays.fill(derived, (byte) 0);\n            }\n        }\n\n        private byte[] dummySaltOfDummy() {\n            StoredDigest self = StoredDigest.parse(dummyEncoded);\n            return self.salt;\n        }\n\n        String policyLabel(Verification v) {\n            return PREFIX + \"$\" + v.iterationsUsed;\n        }\n\n        String policyLabelOf(String encodedDigest) {\n            StoredDigest s = StoredDigest.parse(encodedDigest);\n            return PREFIX + \"$\" + (s == null ? -1 : s.iterations);\n        }\n\n        private char[] randomChars(int count) {\n            final String alphabet =\n                    \"abcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789!#%+-*\";\n            char[] out = new char[count];\n            for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {\n                out[i] = alphabet.charAt(random.nextInt(alphabet.length()));\n            }\n            return out;\n        }\n\n        private static byte[] derive(char[] password, byte[] salt, int rounds) {\n            PBEKeySpec spec = new PBEKeySpec(password, salt, rounds, DIGEST_BYTES * 8);\n            try {\n                SecretKeyFactory factory = SecretKeyFactory.getInstance(KDF);\n                return factory.generateSecret(spec).getEncoded();\n            } catch (NoSuchAlgorithmException | InvalidKeySpecException e) {\n                throw new AuthenticationDataException(\"password hashing unavailable (\" + KDF + \")\", e);\n            } catch (RuntimeException e) {\n                // OutOfMemoryError and friends must not be dressed up as a rejected password.\n                throw e;\n            } finally {\n                spec.clearPassword();\n            }\n        }\n\n        /** Result of one verification. */\n        static final class Verification {\n            private final boolean matched;\n            private final String storedRecordError;\n            private final int iterationsUsed;\n\n            Verification(boolean matched, String storedRecordError, int iterationsUsed) {\n                this.matched = matched;\n                this.storedRecordError = storedRecordError;\n                this.iterationsUsed = iterationsUsed;\n            }\n\n            boolean matched() {\n                return matched;\n            }\n\n            /** {@code null} when the stored record was well formed; otherwise a short code. */\n            String storedRecordError() {\n                return storedRecordError;\n            }\n\n            int iterationsUsed;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Which candidate passwords may be handed to the KDF at all.\n     *\n     * <p>The trailing-NUL and unpaired-surrogate rules are not tidiness. {@code PBEKeySpec} converts\n     * the char[] with a UTF-8 encoder that is not injective: it drops trailing NULs and maps every\n     * unpaired surrogate to '?'. Without these rules \"secret\" and \"secret\\0\" hash identically, so\n     * whoever registered one could be logged in by anyone presenting the other. Rejecting is correct\n     * and trimming is not -- trimming would silently change the secret the user typed.\n     */\n    static final class PasswordRules {\n\n        static final int MIN_ENROLMENT_CHARS = 12;\n        static final int MAX_CHARS = 1024;\n\n        private PasswordRules() {\n        }\n\n        /** Rules that apply to any submitted candidate, at login as well as at enrolment. */\n        static Optional<String> rejectCandidate(char[] candidate) {\n            if (candidate == null || candidate.length == 0) {\n                return Optional.of(\"no-password-submitted\");\n            }\n            if (candidate.length > MAX_CHARS) {\n                return Optional.of(\"password-too-long\");\n            }\n            if (candidate[candidate.length - 1] == '\\0') {\n                return Optional.of(\"password-ends-in-nul\");\n            }\n            for (int i = 0; i < candidate.length; i++) {\n                char c = candidate[i];\n                if (Character.isHighSurrogate(c)) {\n                    if (i + 1 < candidate.length && Character.isLowSurrogate(candidate[i + 1])) {\n                        i++;\n                    } else {\n                        return Optional.of(\"password-has-unpaired-surrogate\");\n                    }\n                } else if (Character.isLowSurrogate(c)) {\n                    return Optional.of(\"password-has-unpaired-surrogate\");\n                }\n            }\n            return Optional.empty();\n        }\n\n        /** Adds the strength floor, which is an enrolment rule only: a legacy account may hold a\n         * shorter password, and refusing to even hash it at login would leak its existence. */\n        static Optional<String> rejectForEnrolment(char[] password) {\n            Optional<String> base = rejectCandidate(password);\n            if (base.isPresent()) {\n                return base;\n            }\n            if (password.length < MIN_ENROLMENT_CHARS) {\n                return Optional.of(\"password-shorter-than-\" + MIN_ENROLMENT_CHARS + \"-characters\");\n            }\n            return Optional.empty();\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Parsed {@code pbkdf2-sha256$...} record. Parsing is strict and reports a short code only --\n     * never an echo of the offending value, because the caller logs the code.\n     */\n    static final class StoredDigest {\n\n        private static final Base64.Decoder STRICT_BASE64 = Base64.getDecoder();\n        private static final ThreadLocal<String> LAST_PARSE_ERROR = new ThreadLocal<>();\n\n        final int iterations;\n        final byte[] salt;\n        final byte[] digest;\n\n        private StoredDigest(int iterations, byte[] salt, byte[] digest) {\n            this.iterations = iterations;\n            this.salt = salt;\n            this.digest = digest;\n        }\n\n        static String lastParseError() {\n            String error = LAST_PARSE_ERROR.get();\n            return error == null ? \"unparsable-record\" : error;\n        }\n\n        static StoredDigest parse(String encoded) {\n            if (encoded == null) {\n                return fail(\"absent-record\");\n            }\n            String[] parts = encoded.split(\"\\\\$\", -1);\n            if (parts.length != 4) {\n                return fail(\"wrong-field-count-\" + parts.length);\n            }\n            if (!PREFIX_MATCH.equals(parts[0])) {\n                return fail(\"unknown-kdf\");\n            }\n            int rounds;\n            try {\n                rounds = Integer.parseInt(parts[1]);\n            } catch (NumberFormatException e) {\n                return fail(\"non-numeric-iterations\");\n            }\n            if (rounds < MIN_ITERATIONS || rounds > MAX_ITERATIONS) {\n                return fail(\"iterations-out-of-range\");\n            }\n            byte[] salt;\n            byte[] digest;\n            try {\n                salt = STRICT_BASE64.decode(parts[2]);\n                digest = STRICT_BASE64.decode(parts[3]);\n            } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {\n                return fail(\"non-base64-material\");\n            }\n            if (salt.length < 8 || salt.length > 128) {\n                return fail(\"salt-length-\" + salt.length);\n            }\n            if (digest.length != DIGEST_BYTES) {\n                return fail(\"digest-length-\" + digest.length);\n            }\n            LAST_PARSE_ERROR.remove();\n            return new StoredDigest(rounds, salt, digest);\n        }\n\n        private static final String PREFIX_MATCH = PasswordHasher.PREFIX;\n        private static final int MIN_ITERATIONS = PasswordHasher.MIN_ITERATIONS;\n        private static final int MAX_ITERATIONS = PasswordHasher.MAX_ITERATIONS;\n        private static final int DIGEST_BYTES = PasswordHasher.DIGEST_BYTES;\n\n        private static StoredDigest fail(String code) {\n            LAST_PARSE_ERROR.set(code);\n            return null;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ============================================================================================\n    // Usernames\n    // ============================================================================================\n\n    /**\n     * Normalisation and syntax gate.\n     *\n     * <p>NFKC before lowercasing so that full-width and other compatibility variants of the same\n     * name cannot resolve to two accounts, {@code Locale.ROOT} so the result does not depend on the\n     * server locale (the Turkish-I case folding bug), and an explicit allow-list so that control\n     * characters, spaces and separators never reach the log or a store key.\n     */\n    static final class Username {\n\n        private static final Pattern ALLOWED = Pattern.compile(\"[a-z0-9._+\\\\-]{1,64}\");\n        private static final int MAX_INPUT_CHARS = 256;\n\n        private final String normalized;\n        private final String invalidReason;\n        private final String rawForLog;\n\n        private Username(String normalized, String invalidReason, String rawForLog) {\n            this.normalized = normalized;\n            this.invalidReason = invalidReason;\n            this.rawForLog = rawForLog;\n        }\n\n        static Username of(String raw) {\n            if (raw == null) {\n                return new Username(null, \"absent\", null);\n            }\n            String stripped = raw.strip();\n            if (stripped.isEmpty()) {\n                return new Username(null, \"empty\", \"\");\n            }\n            if (stripped.length() > MAX_INPUT_CHARS) {\n                return new Username(null, \"longer-than-\" + MAX_INPUT_CHARS + \"-characters\", raw);\n            }\n            if (hasUnpairedSurrogate(stripped)) {\n                return new Username(null, \"malformed-unicode\", raw);\n            }\n            String normalized;\n            try {\n                normalized = Normalizer.normalize(stripped, Normalizer.Form.NFKC)\n                        .toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);\n            } catch (MalformedInputException e) {\n                return new Username(null, \"not-normalisable\", raw);\n            }\n            if (!ALLOWED.matcher(normalized).matches()) {\n                return new Username(null, \"unsupported-characters\", raw);\n            }\n            return new Username(normalized, null, null);\n        }\n\n        private static boolean hasUnpairedSurrogate(String s) {\n            for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {\n                char c = s.charAt(i);\n                if (Character.isHighSurrogate(c)) {\n                    if (i + 1 < s.length() && Character.isLowSurrogate(s.charAt(i + 1))) {\n                        i++;\n                    } else {\n                        return true;\n                    }\n                } else if (Character.isLowSurrogate(c)) {\n                    return true;\n                }\n            }\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        boolean isValid() {\n            return normalized != null;\n        }\n\n        String normalized() {\n            return normalized;\n        }\n\n        String invalidReason() {\n            return invalidReason;\n        }\n\n        /** Normalised name when valid; otherwise the raw input, escaped by the log layer. */\n        String valueForLog() {\n            return isValid() ? normalized : rawForLog;\n        }\n\n        String stateForLog() {\n            if (isValid()) {\n                return \"resolved\";\n            }\n            if (rawForLog == null) {\n                return \"absent\";\n            }\n            return \"malformed(\" + invalidReason + \")\";\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Failures are never reset by another failed attempt, only by a success, an admin\n     * unlock, or the lockout expiring.\n     */\n    public static final class InMemoryFailureTracker implements FailurePolicy {\n\n        private static final class Entry {\n            int consecutiveFailures;\n            Instant lockedUntil;\n        }\n\n        private final Map<String, Entry> byAccountId = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();\n        private final int maxConsecutiveFailures;\n        private final Duration lockout;\n\n        public InMemoryFailureTracker(int maxConsecutiveFailures, Duration lockout) {\n            if (maxConsecutiveFailures < 1) {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"maxConsecutiveFailures must be >= 1\");\n            }\n            if (lockout == null || lockout.isNegative() || lockout.isZero()) {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"lockout must be a positive duration\");\n            }\n            this.maxConsecutiveFailures = maxConsecutiveFailures;\n            this.lockout = lockout;\n        }\n\n        /** Immutable view of the counter state. */\n        public static final class State {\n            private final int consecutiveFailures;\n            private final Instant lockedUntil;\n            private final boolean expiredLockWasCleared;\n\n            State(int consecutiveFailures, Instant lockedUntil, boolean expiredLockWasCleared) {\n                this.consecutiveFailures = consecutiveFailures;\n                this.lockedUntil = lockedUntil;\n                this.expiredLockWasCleared = expiredLockWasCleared;\n            }\n\n            public int consecutiveFailures() {\n                return consecutiveFailures;\n            }\n\n            /** When the lockout ends, or {@code null} when the account is not locked. */\n            public Instant lockedUntil() {\n                return lockedUntil;\n            }\n\n            public boolean locked() {\n                return lockedUntil != null;\n            }\n\n            /** True when this read cleared a lockout that had already expired. */\n            public boolean expiredLockWasCleared() {\n                return expiredLockWasCleared;\n            }\n        }\n\n        /**\n         * Current state. Reading may clear an expired lockout, which is why this takes the clock's\n         * instant rather than caching.\n         */\n        public synchronized State state(String accountId, Instant now) {\n            Entry entry = byAccountId.get(accountId);\n            if (entry == null) {\n                return new State(0, null, false);\n            }\n            if (entry.lockedUntil != null && !entry.lockedUntil.isAfter(now)) {\n                byAccountId.remove(accountId);\n                return new State(0, null, true);\n            }\n            return new State(entry.consecutiveFailures, entry.lockedUntil, false);\n        }\n\n        public synchronized State registerFailure(String accountId, Instant now) {\n            Entry entry = byAccountId.computeIfAbsent(accountId, k -> new Entry());\n            if (entry.lockedUntil != null && !entry.lockedUntil.isAfter(now)) {\n                entry.consecutiveFailures = 0;\n                entry.lockedUntil = null;\n            }\n            entry.consecutiveFailures++;\n            if (entry.lockedUntil == null && entry.consecutiveFailures >= maxConsecutiveFailures) {\n                entry.lockedUntil = now.plus(lockout);\n            }\n            return new State(entry.consecutiveFailures, entry.lockedUntil, false);\n        }\n\n        public synchronized State registerSuccess(String accountId, Instant now) {\n            byAccountId.remove(accountId);\n            return new State(0, null, false);\n        }\n\n        public synchronized State clear(String accountId) {\n            Entry removed = byAccountId.remove(accountId);\n            return removed == null ? new State(0, null, false)\n                    : new State(removed.consecutiveFailures, removed.lockedUntil, false);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ============================================================================================\n    // Audit log\n    // LogValue.escape(operator, 64), before, clock.instant());\n    }\n\n    private AccountRecord requireAccount(String rawUsername) {\n        Username name = Username.of(rawUsername);\n        return name.isValid()\n                ? accounts.find(name.normalized()).orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException(\"no such account\"))\n                : throwNoSuchAccount();\n    }\n\n    private static AccountRecord throwNoSuchAccount() {\n        throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"no such account\");\n    }\n\n    // ============================================================================================\n    // Request / result\n    // ============================================================================================\n\n    /** One authentication attempt as presented by the caller. Immutable. */\n    public static final class LoginRequest {\n\n        private final String rawUsername;\n        private final char[] password;\n        private final String sourceIp;\n        private final String sessionId;\n        private final String userAgent;\n\n        /** Preferred form: the caller keeps a char[] it can erase, and copies the one we store. */\n        public LoginRequest(String rawUsername, char[] password, String sourceIp,\n                            String sessionId, String userAgent) {\n            this.rawUsername = rawUsername;\n            this.password = password == null ? new char[0] : password.clone();\n            this.sourceIp = sourceIp;\n            this.sessionId = sessionId;\n            this.userAgent = userAgent;\n        }\n\n        /** Convenience overload. return sessionId;\n        }\n\n        public String userAgent() {\n            return userAgent;\n        }\n\n        @Override\n        public String toString() {\n            return }\n\n    /** Outcome of one authentication attempt. */\n    public static final class LoginResult {\n\n        private final LoginStatus status;\n        private final String message;\n        private         String accountId, String internalReason) {\n            this.status = status;\n            this.message = message;\n            this.attemptId = attemptId;\n            this.accountId = ============================================================================================\n    // Password hashing\n    // ============================================================================================\n\n    /**\n     * Salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, encoded as\n     * {@code pbkdf2-sha256$<iterations>$<base64 salt>$<base64 digest>}.\n     *\n     * <p>The iteration count is stored per record so it can be raised later without a flag day:\n     * existing records keep verifying at their own cost while new registrations use the new cost.\n     */\n    static final class PasswordHasher {\n\n        static final String KDF = \"PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256\";\n        static final String PREFIX = \"pbkdf2-sha256\";\n        static final int SALT_BYTES = 16;\n        static final int DIGEST_BYTES = 32;\n        static final int DEFAULT_ITERATIONS = 310_000;\n        static final int MIN_ITERATIONS = 1_000;\n        static final int MAX_ITERATIONS = 20_000_000;\n\n        private final SecureRandom random = new SecureRandom();\n        private final int iterations;\n        private final char[] dummyPassword;\n        private final String dummyEncoded;\n        private final byte[] dummySalt;\n\n        PasswordHasher() {\n            this(DEFAULT_ITERATIONS);\n        }\n\n        PasswordHasher(int iterations) {\n            if (iterations < MIN_ITERATIONS || iterations > MAX_ITERATIONS) {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\n                        \"iterations must be in [\" + MIN_ITERATIONS + \", \" + MAX_ITERATIONS + \"]\");\n            }\n            this.iterations = iterations;\n\n            // The digest charged for unknown accounts has to be the product of a real derivation\n            // over a password no account can hold. A hand-written constant is the classic failure\n            // mode: if it does not parse, verify() takes the corrupt-record branch and the\n            // unknown-account path becomes free -- the very leak the constant was meant to close,\n            // with no functional test able to notice. So derive it, then assert it parses.\n            this.dummyPassword = randomChars(24);\n            this.dummyEncoded = deriveEncoded(this.dummyPassword, newSalt(), iterations);\n            StoredDigest parsed = StoredDigest.parse(this.dummyEncoded);\n            if (parsed == null) {\n                throw new IllegalStateException(\"internal error: generated dummy digest does not parse\");\n            }\n            this.dummySalt = parsed.salt;\n        }\n\n        /** Real digest belonging to no account; charged for unknown accounts. */\n        String dummyEncoded() {\n            return dummyEncoded;\n        }\n\n        String encode(char[] password) {\n            PasswordRules.rejectForEnrolment(password).ifPresent(reason -> {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"cannot store this password: \" + reason);\n            });\n            return deriveEncoded(password, newSalt(), iterations);\n        }\n\n        /**\n         * Derives once and compares. Always costs one full derivation, whatever the state of the\n         * inputs: an unparsable stored digest is charged against the dummy parameters, and a\n         * candidate that may not be hashed is replaced by {@code dummyPassword}.\n         */\n        Verification verify(char[] candidate, String storedDigest) {\n            StoredDigest stored = StoredDigest.parse(storedDigest);\n            boolean candidateUsable = PasswordRules.rejectCandidate(candidate).isEmpty();\n\n            char[] effective = candidateUsable ? candidate : dummyPassword;\n            byte[] salt = stored != null ? stored.salt : dummySalt;\n            int rounds = stored != null ? stored.iterations : iterations;\n\n            byte[] derived = derive(effective, salt, rounds);\n            try {\n                // Both operands are always DIGEST_BYTES long, so the comparison leaks nothing about\n                // the stored value beyond \"equal\" or \"not equal\".\n                boolean matched = candidateUsable && stored != null\n                        && MessageDigest.isEqual(stored.digest, derived);\n                String error = stored != null ? null : StoredDigest.lastParseError();\n                return new Verification(matched, error, rounds);\n            } finally {\n                Arrays.fill(derived, (byte) 0);\n            }\n        }\n\n        String policyLabel(Verification verification) {\n            return PREFIX + \"$\" + verification.iterationsUsed();\n        }\n\n        String policyLabelOf(String encodedDigest) {\n            StoredDigest parsed = StoredDigest.parse(encodedDigest);\n            return PREFIX + \"$\" + (parsed == null ? -1 : parsed.iterations);\n        }\n\n        private byte[] newSalt() {\n            byte[] salt = new byte[SALT_BYTES];\n            random.nextBytes(salt);\n            return salt;\n        }\n\n        private String deriveEncoded(char[] password, byte[] salt, int rounds) {\n            byte[] digest = derive(password, salt, rounds);\n            try {\n                return PREFIX + \"$\" + rounds\n                        + \"$\" + Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(salt)\n                        + \"$\" + Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(digest);\n            } finally {\n                Arrays.fill(digest, (byte) 0);\n            }\n        }\n\n        private char[] randomChars(int count) {\n            final String alphabet = \"abcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789!#*+-\";\n            char[] out = new char[count];\n            for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {\n                out[i] = alphabet.charAt(random.nextInt(alphabet.length()));\n            }\n            return out;\n        }\n\n        private static byte[] derive(char[] password, byte[] salt, int rounds) {\n            PBEKeySpec spec = new PBEKeySpec(password, salt, rounds, DIGEST_BYTES * 8);\n            try {\n                SecretKeyFactory factory = SecretKeyFactory.getInstance(KDF);\n                return factory.generateSecret(spec).getEncoded();\n            } catch (NoSuchAlgorithmException | InvalidKeySpecException e) {\n                throw new AuthenticationDataException(\"password hashing unavailable (\" + KDF + \")\", e);\n            } finally {\n                spec.clearPassword();\n            }\n        }\n\n        /** Result of one verification. */\n        static final class Verification {\n\n            private final boolean matched;\n            private final String storedRecordError;\n            private final int iterationsUsed;\n\n            Verification(boolean matched, String storedRecordError, int iterationsUsed) {\n                this.matched = matched;\n                this.storedRecordError = storedRecordError;\n                this.iterationsUsed = iterationsUsed;\n            }\n\n            boolean matched() {\n                return matched;\n            }\n\n            /** {@code null} when the stored record was well formed, otherwise a short code. */\n            String storedRecordError() {\n                return storedRecordError;\n            }\n\n            int iterationsUsed() {\n                return iterationsUsed;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Which candidate passwords may be handed to the KDF at all.\n     *\n     * <p>The trailing-NUL and unpaired-surrogate rules are not tidiness. {@code PBEKeySpec} converts\n     * the char[] with a UTF-8 encoder that is not injective over the whole char[] domain: it drops\n     * trailing NULs and maps every unpaired surrogate to '?'. Without these rules \"correcthorse\"\n     * and \"correcthorse\\0\" produce the same digest, so whoever registered one could be logged in by\n     * anyone presenting the other. Rejecting is the right response; trimming would silently change\n     * the secret the user actually typed.\n     */\n    static final class PasswordRules {\n\n        static final int MIN_ENROLMENT_CHARS = 12;\n        static final int MAX_CHARS = 1024;\n\n        private PasswordRules() {\n        }\n\n        /** Rules that apply to any submitted candidate, at login as well as at enrolment. */\n        static Optional<String> rejectCandidate(char[] candidate) {\n            if (candidate == null || candidate.length == 0) {\n                return Optional.of(\"no-password-submitted\");\n            }\n            if (candidate.length > MAX_CHARS) {\n                return Optional.of(\"password-too-long\");\n            }\n            if (candidate[candidate.length - 1] == '\\0') {\n                return Optional.of(\"password-ends-in-nul\");\n            }\n            for (int i = 0; i < candidate.length; i++) {\n                char c = candidate[i];\n                if (Character.isHighSurrogate(c)) {\n                    if (i + 1 < candidate.length && Character.isLowSurrogate(candidate[i + 1])) {\n                        i++;\n                    } else {\n                        return Optional.of(\"password-has-unpaired-surrogate\");\n                    }\n                } else if (Character.isLowSurrogate(c)) {\n                    return Optional.of(\"password-has-unpaired-surrogate\");\n                }\n            }\n            return Optional.empty();\n        }\n\n        /**\n         * Adds the strength floor, which is an enrolment rule only. A legacy account may legitimately\n         * hold a shorter password, and refusing to hash it at login would turn policy into an\n         * enumeration channel.\n         */\n        static Optional<String> rejectForEnrolment(char[] password) {\n            Optional<String> base = rejectCandidate(password);\n            if (base.isPresent()) {\n                return base;\n            }\n            if (password.length < MIN_ENROLMENT_CHARS) {\n                return Optional.of(\"password-shorter-than-\" + MIN_ENROLMENT_CHARS + \"-characters\");\n            }\n            return Optional.empty();\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Parsed {@code pbkdf2-sha256$...} record. Parsing is strict and reports a short code only --\n     * never an echo of the offending value, because the caller writes the code into the log.\n     */\n    static final class StoredDigest {\n\n        private static final Base64.Decoder STRICT_BASE64 = Base64.getDecoder();\n        private static final ThreadLocal<String> LAST_PARSE_ERROR = new ThreadLocal<>();\n\n        final int iterations;\n        final byte[] salt;\n        final byte[] digest;\n\n        private StoredDigest(int iterations, byte[] salt, byte[] digest) {\n            this.iterations = iterations;\n            this.salt = salt;\n            this.digest = digest;\n        }\n\n        static String lastParseError() {\n            String error = LAST_PARSE_ERROR.get();\n            return error == null ? \"unparsable-record\" : error;\n        }\n\n        static StoredDigest parse(String encoded) {\n            if (encoded == null) {\n                return fail(\"absent-record\");\n            }\n            String[] parts = encoded.split(\"\\\\$\", -1);\n            if (parts.length != 4) {\n                return fail(\"wrong-field-count-\" + parts.length);\n            }\n            if (!PasswordHasher.PREFIX.equals(parts[0])) {\n                return fail(\"unknown-kdf\");\n            }\n            int rounds;\n            try {\n                rounds = Integer.parseInt(parts[1]);\n            } catch (NumberFormatException e) {\n                return fail(\"non-numeric-iterations\");\n            }\n            if (rounds < PasswordHasher.MIN_ITERATIONS || rounds > PasswordHasher.MAX_ITERATIONS) {\n                return fail(\"iterations-out-of-range\");\n            }\n            byte[] salt;\n            byte[] digest;\n            try {\n                salt = STRICT_BASE64.decode(parts[2]);\n                digest = STRICT_BASE64.decode(parts[3]);\n            } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {\n                return fail(\"non-base64-material\");\n            }\n            if (salt.length < 8 || salt.length > 128) {\n                return fail(\"salt-length-\" + salt.length);\n            }\n            if (digest.length != PasswordHasher.DIGEST_BYTES) {\n                return fail(\"digest-length-\" + digest.length);\n            }\n            LAST_PARSE_ERROR.remove();\n            return new StoredDigest(rounds, salt, digest);\n        }\n\n        private static StoredDigest fail(String code) {\n            LAST_PARSE_ERROR.set(code);\n            return null;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ============================================================================================\n    // Usernames\n    // ============================================================================================\n\n    /**\n     * Normalisation and syntax gate.\n     *\n     * <p>NFKC before lowercasing, so compatibility variants of one name (full-width letters and the\n     * like) cannot become two different accounts; {@code Locale.ROOT}, so the result does not depend\n     * on the server locale (the Turkish-I case-folding bug); and an explicit allow-list, so control\n     * characters, spaces and separators never reach the log or a store key.\n     */\n    static final class Username {\n\n        private static final Pattern ALLOWED = Pattern.compile(\"[a-z0-9._+\\\\-]{1,64}\");\n        private static final int MAX_INPUT_CHARS = 256;\n\n        private final String normalized;\n        private final String invalidReason;\n        private final String rawForLog;\n\n        private Username(String normalized, String invalidReason, String rawForLog) {\n            this.normalized = normalized;\n            this.invalidReason = invalidReason;\n            this.rawForLog = rawForLog;\n        }\n\n        static Username of(String raw) {\n            if (raw == null) {\n                return new Username(null, \"absent\", null);\n            }\n            String stripped = raw.strip();\n            if (stripped.isEmpty()) {\n                return new Username(null, \"empty\", raw);\n            }\n            if (stripped.length() > MAX_INPUT_CHARS) {\n                return new Username(null, \"longer-than-\" + MAX_INPUT_CHARS + \"-characters\", raw);\n            }\n            if (hasUnpairedSurrogate(stripped)) {\n                return new Username(null, \"malformed-unicode\", raw);\n            }\n            String normalized;\n            try {\n                normalized = Normalizer.normalize(stripped, Normalizer.Form.NFKC).toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);\n            } catch (MalformedInputException e) {\n                return new Username(null, \"not-normalisable\", raw);\n            }\n            if (!ALLOWED.matcher(normalized).matches()) {\n                return new Username(null, \"unsupported-characters\", raw);\n            }\n            return new Username(normalized, null, null);\n        }\n\n        private static boolean hasUnpairedSurrogate(String s) {\n            for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {\n                char c = s.charAt(i);\n                if (Character.isHighSurrogate(c)) {\n                    if (i + 1 < s.length() && Character.isLowSurrogate(s.charAt(i + 1))) {\n                        i++;\n                    } else {\n                        return true;\n                    }\n                } else if (Character.isLowSurrogate(c)) {\n                    return true;\n                }\n            }\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        boolean isValid() {\n            return normalized != null;\n        }\n\n        String normalized() {\n            return normalized;\n        }\n\n        String invalidReason() {\n            return invalidReason;\n        }\n\n        /** Normalised name when valid; otherwise the raw input, escaped by the log layer. */\n        String valueForLog() {\n            return isValid() ? normalized : rawForLog;\n        }\n\n        String stateForLog() {\n            return isValid() ? \"resolved\" : \"malformed(\" + invalidReason + \")\";\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ============================================================================================\n    // Accounts\n    // ============================================================================================\n\n    enum AccountStatus {\n        ACTIVE,\n        DISABLED,\n        LOCKED_BY_ADMIN;\n\n        String logToken() {\n            return name().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT).replace('_', '-');\n        }\n    }\n\n    /** Immutable stored account. {@link #toString()} never exposes the credential. */\n    static final class AccountRecord {\n\n        private final String accountId;\n        private final String username;\n        private final String passwordHash;\n        private final AccountStatus      void store(AccountRecord account);\n    }\n\n    /** Process-local store, adequate for the demo and the tests. */\n    public static final class InMemoryAccountStore implements AccountStore {\n\n        private final Map<String, AccountRecord> byUsername = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();\n\n        @Override\n        public Optional<AccountRecord> find(String normalisedUsername) {\n            return Optional.ofNullable(byUsername.get(normalisedUsername));\n        }\n\n        @Override\n        public boolean exists(String normalisedUsername) {\n            return public String toString() {\n            return \"InMemoryAccountStore\" + byUsername.keySet();\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ============================================================================================\n    // Lockout\n    // ============================================================================================\n\n    /**\n     * Counts consecutive failures per account id and applies a time-boxed lockout.\n     *\n     * <p>Keyed by account id rather than username, so no spelling variant can split the counter.\n     * The count is never reset by another failure -- only by a success, an administrative unlock, or\n     * the lockout expiring.\n     */\n    public static final class InMemoryFailureTracker {\n\n        private static final class Entry {\n            int consecutiveFailures;\n            Instant lockedUntil;\n        }\n\n        /** Immutable view of counter state. */\n        public static final class State {\n\n            private final int consecutiveFailures;\n            private final Instant lockedUntil;\n            private final boolean expiredLockWasCleared;\n\n            State(int consecutiveFailures, Instant lockedUntil, boolean expiredLockWasCleared) {\n                this.consecutiveFailures = consecutiveFailures;\n                this.lockedUntil = lockedUntil;\n                this.expiredLockWasCleared = expiredLockWasCleared;\n            }\n\n            public int consecutiveFailures() {\n                return consecutiveFailures;\n            }\n\n            /** When the lockout ends, or {@code null} when the account is not locked. */\n            public Instant lockedUntil() {\n                return lockedUntil;\n            }\n\n            public boolean locked() {\n                return lockedUntil != null;\n            }\n\n            /** True when this read cleared a lockout that had already expired. */\n            public boolean expiredLockWasCleared() {\n                return expiredLockWasCleared;\n            }\n        }\n\n        private final Map<String, Entry> byAccountId = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();\n        private final int maxConsecutiveFailures;\n        private final Duration lockout;\n\n        public InMemoryFailureTracker(int maxConsecutiveFailures, Duration lockout) {\n            if (maxConsecutiveFailures < 1) {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"maxConsecutiveFailures must be >= 1\");\n            }\n            if (lockout == null || lockout.isNegative() || lockout.isZero()) {\n                throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"lockout must be a positive duration\");\n            }\n            this.maxConsecutiveFailures = maxConsecutiveFailures;\n            this.lockout = lockout;\n        }\n\n        public int maxConsecutiveFailures() {\n            return maxConsecutiveFailures;\n        }\n\n        public Duration lockout() {\n            return lockout;\n        }\n\n        /**\n         * Current state. Reading may clear an expired lockout, which is why the caller supplies the\n         * instant instead of caching the result.\n         */\n        public synchronized State state(String accountId, Instant now) {\n            Entry entry = byAccountId.get(accountId);\n            if (entry == null) {\n                return new State(0, null, false);\n            }\n            if (entry.lockedUntil != null && !entry.lockedUntil.isAfter(now)) {\n                byAccountId.remove(accountId);\n                return new State(0, null, true);\n            }\n            return new State(entry.consecutiveFailures, entry.lockedUntil, false);\n        }\n\n        public synchronized State registerFailure(String accountId, Instant now) {\n            Entry entry = byAccountId.computeIfAbsent(accountId, key -> new Entry());\n            if (entry.lockedUntil != null && !entry.lockedUntil.isAfter(now)) {\n                entry.consecutiveFailures = 0;\n                entry.lockedUntil = null;\n            }\n            entry.consecutiveFailures++;\n            if (entry.lockedUntil == null && entry.consecutiveFailures >= maxConsecutiveFailures) {\n                entry.lockedUntil = now.plus(lockout);\n            }\n            return new State(entry.consecutiveFailures, entry.lockedUntil, false);\n        }\n\n        public synchronized State registerSuccess(String accountId, Instant now) {\n            byAccountId.remove(accountId);\n            return new State(0, null, false);\n        }\n\n        public synchronized State clear(String accountId) {\n            Entry removed = byAccountId.remove(accountId);\n            return removed == null\n                    ? new State(0, null, false)\n                    : new State(removed.consecutiveFailures, removed.lockedUntil, false);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ============================================================================================\n    // Audit log\n    // ============================================================================================\n\n    /** Everything known about one attempt, assembled as the attempt proceeds, rendered once at the end. */\n    static final class LoginContext {\n\n        private final String attemptId;\n        private final String sourceIp;\n        private final String sessionId;\n        private final private Instant lockedUntil;\n        private Instant previousSuccessAt;\n        private String previousSuccessIp;\n        private String policy;\n        private final Map<String, String> details = new LinkedHashMap<>();\n\n        LoginContext(String attemptId, String sourceIp, String sessionId, String userAgent) {\n            this.attemptId = attemptId;\n            this.sourceIp = sourceIp;\n            this.sessionId = sessionId;\n            this.userAgent = userAgent;\n        }\n\n        String attemptId() {\n            return attemptId;\n        }\n\n        String this.subjectState = state;\n        }\n\n        void account(AccountRecord record) {\n            this.account = record;\n        }\n\n        void consecutiveFailures(int value) {\n *   <li>C0/C1 controls, DEL, U+0085, U+00A0 and U+2028/U+2029 are percent-encoded.</li>\n     * </ul>\n     * What remains is printable ASCII; if it still contains whitespace the whole value is   static String escape(String raw, int maxChars) {\n            if (raw == null) {\n                return \"-\";\n            }\n            int limit = Math.min(raw.length(), Math.max(0, maxChars));\n            StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder(limit + 16);\n            int i = 0;\n            while (i < limit) {\n                int cp = raw.codePointAt(i);\n                int width = Character.charCount(cp);\n                if (i + width > limit) {\n                    break;\n                }\n                i += width;\n                if (cp == '%') {\n                    out.append(\"%25\");\n                } else if (cp == '\"') {\n                    out.append(\"%22\");\n                } else if (cp == '\\\\') {\n                    out.append(\"%5C\");\n (byte) cp });\n                } else if (isDangerousNonAscii(cp)) {\n                    appendPercentEncoded(out, new String(Character.toChars(cp))\n                            .getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));\n                } else {\n                    appendPercentEncoded(out, new String(Character.toChars(cp))\n                            .getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));\n                }\n            }\n            if (limit < raw.length()) {\n                out.append(\"(+truncated)\");\n            }\n            String escaped = out.toString();\n            boolean needsQuoting = escaped.chars().anyMatch(Character::isWhitespace);\n            return needsQuoting ? '\"' + escaped + '\"' : escaped;\n        }\n\n        /**\n         * Everything at or above 0x80 is percent-encoded regardless of category, so the emitted line\n         * is pure ASCII. Tracker and concurrency\n    // ============================================================================================\n\n    private static void failureTrackerUnitBehaviour() {\n        Instant t0 = Instant.parse(\"2026-09-12T00:00:00Z\");\n        AuthService.InMemoryFailureTracker tracker =\n                new AuthService.InMemoryFailureTracker(2, Duration.ofMinutes(5));\n\n        check(\"a fresh account has no state\",\n                tracker.state(\"a\", t0).consecutiveFailures() == 0 && !tracker.state(\"a\", t0).locked());\n        check(\"one failure is below the threshold\",\n                !tracker.registerFailure(\"a\", t0).locked());\n        check(\"the second failure locks\", tracker.registerFailure(\"a\", t0).locked());\n        check(\"the deadline is now plus the window\",\n                tracker.state(\"a\", t0).lockedUntil().equals(t0.plus(Duration.ofMinutes(5))));\n        check(\"further failures do not extend the deadline\",\n                tracker.registerFailure(\"a\", t0).lockedUntil().equals(t0.plus(Duration.ofMinutes(5))));\n        check(\"a success clears everything\",\n                !tracker.registerSuccess(\"a\", t0).locked()\n                        && tracker.state(\"a\", t0).consecutiveFailures() == 0);\n\n        tracker.registerFailure(\"b\", t0);\n        tracker.registerFailure(\"b\", t0);\n        check(\"state() reports the live lockout\", tracker.state(\"b\", t0).locked());\n        AuthService.InMemoryFailureTracker.State afterExpiry =\n                tracker.state(\"b\", t0.plus(Duration.ofMinutes(6)));\n        check(\"an expired lockout reads as unlocked\", !afterExpiry.locked());\n        check(\"and the read says it cleared it\", afterExpiry.expiredLockWasCleared());\n\n        tracker.registerFailure(\"c\", t0);\n        tracker.registerFailure(\"c\", t0);\n        check(\"clear() removes the lockout\", !tracker.clear(\"c\").locked() && !tracker.state(\"c\", t0).locked());\n        check(\"a tracker rejects a nonsense threshold\",\n                throwsIllegalArgument(() -> new AuthService.InMemoryFailureTracker(0, Duration.ofMinutes(1))));\n        check(\"a tracker rejects a zero lockout window\",\n                throwsIllegalArgument(() -> new AuthService.InMemoryFailureTracker(3, Duration.ZERO)));\n    }\n\n    private static void concurrentAttemptsAreCountedAndLogged() throws Exception {\n        Harness h = new Harness(FAST_ITERATIONS, 1_000_000, Duration.ofMinutes(15));\n        h.capture.clear();\n        int threads = 16;\n        CountDownLatch start = new CountDownLatch(1);\n        CountDownLatch done = new CountDownLatch(threads);\n        AtomicInteger failuresSeen = new AtomicInteger();\n        List<Thread> pool = new ArrayList<>();\n        for (int i = 0; i < threads; i++) {\n            final int index = i;\n            Thread worker = new Thread(() -> {\n                try {\n                    start.await();\n                    if (!h.login(\"alice\", \"concurrent-bad-\" + index).authenticated()) {\n                        failuresSeen.incrementAndGet();\n                    }\n                } catch (InterruptedException e) {\n                    Thread.currentThread().interrupt();\n                } finally {\n                    done.countDown();\n                }\n            });\n            pool.add(worker);\n JDK only — no third-party dependencies, no build tool.\n\nFiles:\n\n| File | Purpose |\n| --- | --- |\n| `AuthService.java` | The implementation, plus a runnable demo (`AuthService.main`). |\n| `AuthServiceTest.java` | 233 verification checks, no test framework required. |\n\n## Build and run\n\n```bash\njavac -d out AuthService.java AuthServiceTest.java     # compiles clean under -Xlint:all -Werror\n\njava -cp out AuthService                # scripted scenario, prints the audit log as it is written\njava -cp out AuthService login          # one interactive login (needs a real terminal)\njava -cp out AuthServiceTest            # the verification suite; exits non-zero on failure\n```\n\nRequirements: JDK 17 or newer (`java -version` was 17.0.20.1 here). Sources are ASCII-only, so no\n`-encoding` flag is needed, and the audit log is pure ASCII, so it survives any console.\n\n`AuthService` writes the audit log to **`./auth.log`** (appending) and echoes it to stdout. Run from\na directory you don't mind that file appearing in.\n\n## What a login does\n\n```java\nAuthService service = new AuthService(\n        new AuthService.InMemoryAccountStore(),\n        new AuthService.PasswordHasher(310_000),                        // PBKDF2 iterations\n        new AuthService.InMemoryFailureTracker(5, Duration.ofMinutes(15)),\n        new AuthService.AuthAuditLogger(),                              // java.util.logging \"auth.audit\"\n        Clock.systemUTC());\n\nservice.register(\"alice\", \"correct-horse-battery\".toCharArray());\n\nAuthService.LoginResult result = service.login(new AuthService.LoginRequest(\n        \"alice\", passwordChars, \"203.0.113.10\", \"sess-42\", \"Mozilla/5.0 ...\"));\n\nif (result.authenticated()) {\n    issueSession(result.accountId());\n}\n```\n\n`login()` never throws because of a wrong password. It throws\n`AuthService.AuthenticationDataException` only when a stored credential cannot be parsed — that\naccount cannot be judged at all, and answering \"wrong password\" would hide a broken import.\n\nThe subject always gets one of exactly two sentences: `Authenticated.`, or\n\n> Authentication failed. The username and password provided could not be verified.\n\nThe real reason is never in that sentence. It is available to the caller through\n`LoginResult.internalReason()` for counters and alerting, and it is on the audit line.\n\n## What the log records\n\nOne record per attempt — including the attempt that trips a lockout, which is the same record\nescalated to `WARNING` rather than a second line, so a dashboard counting records counts attempts.\n\n```\n2026-09-12T04:35:35.697Z INFO  auth.audit event=AUTH_SUCCESS outcome=SUCCESS reason=authenticated\n  attempt=28b72ce23784 subject=alice subjectState=resolved account=acct-c8b5d48b2d accountState=active\n  ip=203.0.113.10 session=sess-1 agent=\"DemoClient/1.0 (scenario runner)\" failures=0 lockedUntil=-\n  previousSuccess=- previousSuccessIp=- policy=pbkdf2-sha256$60000 elapsedMs=89\n```\n\nThe header is `UTC-timestamp LEVEL logger-name`, then ordered `key=value` fields. Absent values are\nwritten as `-` rather than omitted, so every record has the same shape and a parser never has to\nguess whether a missing field means \"no value\" or \"older format\".\n\n| Field | Why an investigator needs it |\n| --- | --- |\n| `event` | `AUTH_SUCCESS`, `AUTH_FAILURE`, `ACCOUNT_CREATED`, `ACCOUNT_STATUS_CHANGED`, `ACCOUNT_UNLOCKED`, `CREDENTIAL_RECORD_CORRUPT`. |\n| `outcome` | `SUCCESS` / `FAILURE` / `INFO` (administrative records). Cheap filter. |\n| `reason` | The precise cause. **Internal**: `password-mismatch`, `password-mismatch-locking`, `unknown-account`, `account-locked`, `account-disabled`, `account-locked-by-admin`, `username-unsupported-characters` (and siblings), `password-ends-in-nul`, `password-has-unpaired-surrogate`, `password-too-long`, `no-password-submitted`. |\n| `attempt` | Correlation id, 12 hex chars. The same value the subject was shown in `LoginResult.attemptId()`, which is what lets a support ticket be matched to a line without guessing. Administrative records use an `admin-<epoch>-<micros>` id. |\n| `subject` | The name that was *typed*. Normalised when it parses (`ALICE ` → `alice`), otherwise the raw input, escaped. Recording the raw attempt is what makes credential-stuffing and probe traffic visible. |\n| `subjectState` | `resolved`, or `malformed(<cause>)` — `empty`, `absent`, `unsupported-characters`, `malformed-unicode`, `longer-than-256-characters`. Separates a real account miss from malformed input. |\n| `account` | Account id, or `-`. The join key across accounts, devices and log files, stable across renames. |\n| `accountState` | `active`, `disabled`, `locked-by-admin`, or `no-such-account`. |\n| `ip`, `session`, `agent` | Where it came from. Client-supplied, so escaped like `subject`; the `ip` alone should never be trusted for a decision. |\n| `failures` | Consecutive-failure counter *as it stood when the attempt was judged* (post-increment on a mismatch). `0` after a success; `-` when no account was identified. |\n| `lockedUntil` | When a lockout ends — the answer to \"when can the user try again\", and the evidence that a lockout did *not* slide forward on every locked attempt. |\n| `previousSuccess`, `previousSuccessIp` | The account's last good login **and its address**, carried on failure lines too. This is what distinguishes \"the user typoed\" from \"someone who is not this user started trying\", and it is only useful if it is on the *failure* record. |\n| `policy` | The KDF and the iteration count actually charged, e.g. `pbkdf2-sha256$310000`. Makes a cost-raise rollout, or a downgraded record, visible in the log. |\n| `recordError` | On `CREDENTIAL_RECORD_CORRUPT` only: the specific parse failure (`unknown-kdf`, `digest-length-20`, `non-base64-material`, …) so the operator can find the bad row. |\n| `elapsedMs` | Wall time of the attempt. Operational signal, and the continuous evidence that the equal-cost derivation below really ran. |\n| `fromState`/`toState`, `createdAt`, `operator` | On the administrative records: who changed what, and when the account appeared. |\n\nLevels are chosen so a collector can alert without string matching: **INFO** for ordinary successes\nand refusals, **WARNING** for the attempt that crossed the lockout threshold, **SEVERE** for a\ncorrupt stored credential.\n\n### Log adequacy is checked, not asserted in prose\n\n`AuthServiceTest` proves the log claims above rather than describing them:\n\n- exactly one record per attempt, across five different refusal shapes, with unique attempt ids;\n- the record's `attempt` equals the id in the result handed to the subject;\n- every investigative field present and correct on success, wrong-password, unknown-account,\n  disabled, locked and corrupt-record records;\n- **no password anywhere in any emitted string**, and no stored digest either;\n- a username containing `\\n` plus a forged `event=AUTH_SUCCESS outcome=SUCCESS` payload produces\n  **one** record, whose parsed `event`/`outcome`/`reason`/`account` are the real ones;\n- non-ASCII input is recoverable byte-for-byte from the escaping, and the line is pure ASCII;\n- oversized input is truncated *and says so* (`(+truncated)`).\n\n### Escaping rules\n\nFree-text values (`subject`, `ip`, `session`, `agent`) pass through one escaping function:\n\n1. `%`, `\"` and `\\` are percent-encoded — the escape language itself cannot be forged;\n2. every byte of every non-ASCII code point is percent-encoded via UTF-8, which keeps the line pure\n   ASCII and keeps a look-alike Unicode username exactly reproducible;\n3. C0/C1 controls, DEL and U+2028/U+2029 are therefore encoded too;\n4. what remains is printable ASCII; if it still contains whitespace the value is quoted.\n\nSo `agent=\"DemoClient/1.0 (scenario runner)\"` is one field, and an injected newline appears as\n`%0A` inside a single value.\n\n## Security properties, and how each is pinned\n\n| Property | Mechanism | Check |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| No plaintext passwords stored, logged or echoed | Passwords travel as `char[]`, are defensively copied, and the copy is zeroed when the attempt ends; `toString()` on request and record redacts | 3 checks in `noSecretInAnyEmittedString`, `callerOwnedBuffersAreNotClobbered`, `password-not-wiped`/`*-leaks` mutants |\n| No user enumeration **by response text** | One generic sentence for all seven refusal shapes | `publicMessageIsIdenticalForEveryRefusal` (also asserts the sentence contains no hint words) |\n| No user enumeration **by timing** | Exactly **one** key derivation per attempt on every path: an unknown account is charged against a *real* digest that no login can match; an unusable candidate is swapped for a random password belonging to nobody | `everyRefusalShapeCostsTheSameWork` times all five early-return shapes, and asserts an absolute floor as well as a ratio window |\n| No enumeration via the **log's** timing column | `elapsedMs` is written from the same measured span, and checked to be comparable | asserted directly from the parsed records |\n| A corrupt credential is never \"wrong password\" | `AuthenticationDataException` + SEVERE `CREDENTIAL_RECORD_CORRUPT` with `recordError` | `corruptCredentialIsDataFault` |\n| Distinct passwords cannot collide | `PBEKeySpec` is **not** injective over `char[]`: it drops trailing NULs and maps every unpaired surrogate to `?`, so `\"pw\"` and `\"pw\\0\"` would hash identically. Such candidates are rejected, never silently trimmed | `unusableCandidatesAreRejected`; `nul-collision-allowed` / `trailing-nul-rule-removed` / `surrogate-rule-removed` mutants |\n| Credentials are salted, per-record-cost, constant-compared | `pbkdf2-sha256$<iters>$<b64 salt>$<b64 digest>`, 16-byte random salt per record, `MessageDigest.isEqual` over two fixed-length 32-byte digests | `hashFormatAndSalting`, `storedDigestParsingIsStrict`, `no-per-record-iterations` / `no-salt-per-record` mutants |\n| Brute force is bounded | Consecutive failures per **account id** (not username spelling), lockout for a bounded window, correct passwords refused during the window, expiry automatic, failures not counted during a lockout and the deadline does not slide | `failureCounterProgression`, `thresholdCrossingIsOneWarningRecord`, `correctPasswordDuringLockoutIsRefused`, `lockoutExpires`, `failureTrackerUnitBehaviour` |\n| One username cannot be two accounts | NFKC then `toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)`, then an explicit allow-list `[a-z0-9._+\\-]{1,64}` | `usernameNormalisation` (full-width `ａｌｉｃｅ` resolves to `alice`; The constructor derives the value at startup and *asserts\n  it parses*; the timing test re-checks the cost. Startup pays one extra derivation.\n- **`java.util.logging`** keeps the file dependency-free. `AuthAuditLogger` wraps a named logger\n  (`auth.audit`) and `IsoLogFormatter` renders one ASCII line per record, so wiring in Log4j2 or\n  Logback later is a handler swap, not a rewrite — and a JSON layout then gets the same field names.\n- **`Clock` is injected**, which is what makes lockout expiry testable without sleeping.\n- **The failure tracker is process-local.** In a real deployment it belongs in a shared store\n  (database, Redis); the interface boundary is already drawn at `InMemoryFailureTracker`, and the\n  counter is keyed by account id so it is already rename-proof.\n\n## Known limitations\n\nDeliberate boundaries, not oversights:\n\n- **No rate limiting per source address or per session** — only per-account lockout. A slow\n  credential-stuffing run spread across many usernames is not impeded. Add an IP/session budget in\n  front of this.\n- **No password change, reset or MFA.** `AccountStore.recordFor(username)` exists precisely so a\n  rehash-on-cost-raise or reset flow can read the stored record and `store()` a replacement without\n  racing another writer.\n- **`InMemoryAccountStore` and `InMemoryFailureTracker` are process-local** — for the demo and the\n  tests. Implement `AccountStore` (three lookups plus `store`) to put this behind a database.\n- **Lockout is time-boxed, not permanent**, and the counter resets on expiry. That is a\n  usability/security trade; a permanent admin unlock is a one-line policy change in\n  `InMemoryFailureTracker`.\n- **`ip`/`session`/`agent` are trusted inputs for *recording*, never for *deciding*.** They are\n  escaped like any other input and should be populated by the transport layer, not by the client.\n- **PBKDF2 is a defensible floor, not the strongest option.** The encoding carries a `kdf` field and\n  a per-record cost, so migrating to Argon2id or scrypt is an additive change; `MIN_ITERATIONS`\n  guards against a record importing a cost that is too cheap to accept.\n- Single-file package-private layout, chosen for reviewability — no DI container, no configuration\n  file.
